newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit breaches 2.50/dlr on overseas selling.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit breaches 2.50/dlr on overseas selling.

text.p: Continued selling out of Singapore by speculators and some Malaysian sources pushed the ringgit above 2.50/dollar psychological level, dealers said.
They said the ringgit was expected to decline further next week, with the next support for it pegged at 2.5050.
One Malaysian bank dealer said the support for the ringgit in the last few days was from European hedge funds in London, but this was being overshadowed by selling out of Singapore.
At 0830 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5004/18 per dollar against 2.4985/95 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Thursday. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5632/34 against 0.5626/36.
"There is a lot of dollar shortcovering. On the whole there is a negative view towards the ringgit," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market was eagerly waiting for Malaysia's July trade data, which government officials told Reuters would not be released today.
The market widely expects a large trade deficit ranging from 500 million to one billion ringgit.
In a poll by Reuters, economists from nine research houses said the trade deficit in 1996 would be an average 4.95 billion ringgit against 8.55 billion forecast three months ago.
